Summary
Jack writes to Folks and Ruth about the cancellation of a trip due to the demobilization program. He mentions the shipping situation in the Philippines and the election results. He also discusses the War Department's reluctance to speed up demobilization and the suspicion of U.S. involvement in China. The tone is informative and somewhat concerned.

--- Page 1 (Beckerman_54a) --- Dear Folks and Ruth; another peaceful Sunday coming around marks the time for a letter to you. Received one from you this week. Very little news to relate. By the way, I think I wrote you a little of a trip I was expecting to make. Well, this is to let you know that the trip has been called off. Everyone here is concentrating on the demobilization program. You have probably read in the papers of the terrible shipping situation in the Philippines as usual. Don't think I told you that I filled out my election ballot some time ago and was happy to see O'Dwyer [illegible] to the N.Y.C. mayoralty. Had tickets to see the Yankees but tried without them. was postponed! Expect to [illegible] --- Page 2 (Beckerman_54b) --- It again next week. Many of my old friends are going home. Most all of the faces are new and unfamiliar. There are plenty of replacements for everyone. But the War Department does not seem too anxious to speed demobilization. It's a nasty situation. People here are very suspicious of the meaning of U.S. meddling in China. Is that an attempt to keep larger forces out here? That's about all for today folks. Love and regards. Jack.
